summary: Hà Nam is the gateway province south of Hà Nội, famous for the cá kho braised in a niêu đất (clay pot) from làng Vũ Đại, the village of Nam Cao's fiction, along with chuối ngự Đại Hoàng — a banana once chosen as tribute to the king — and simple breakfast dishes such as bánh cuốn Phủ Lý. The cooking here is thoroughly Red River Delta, drawing carefully on the produce of the Châu and Đáy rivers.

ca-kho-lang-vu-dai.description: Cá kho làng Vũ Đại is the speciality of Nhân Hậu village (formerly Đại Hoàng) in Hòa Hậu commune, Lý Nhân district, Hà Nam — the village bound up with the writing of Nam Cao. The fish is kho (braised in a dark savoury caramel) inside a niêu đất (clay pot) over a wood fire for many hours, giving a deep flavour, bones soft enough to eat and flesh that stays firm, scented with riềng (galangal) and ginger.
keyIngredients: Cá trắm đen (black carp), or cá trắm cỏ (grass carp)
Lime juice, or quả chay and quả dọc (local sour fruits)
Nước hàng (caramel sauce) and good nước mắm (Vietnamese fish sauce)
A niêu đất (clay pot) with a lá chuối (banana leaf) lid
prepOutline: Choose fresh cá trắm đen (black carp), clean it and cut it into thick sections
Line the bottom of the niêu đất (clay pot) with riềng (galangal) and ginger, then lay the fish on top
Marinate the fish with nước mắm (Vietnamese fish sauce), nước hàng (caramel sauce) and seasonings for a few hours
Braise over a low wood fire for 10-12 hours until the liquid has cooked away and the bones are meltingly soft
ca-kho-lang-vu-dai.howToEat: The cá kho is eaten hot with plain rice, and is especially common on the Tết tray in Hà Nam households; at the end of the year it is ordered as a gift and sent all over the country.

chuoi-ngu-dai-hoang.description: Chuối ngự Đại Hoàng is a small-fruited, exceptionally fragrant banana grown in Đại Hoàng village (now Nhân Hậu) in Hòa Hậu commune, Lý Nhân district, Hà Nam — where the Trần kings chose it as tribute, which is how it got its name. The ripe fruit has a glossy yellow skin and deeply sweet yellow flesh with a gentle fragrance, quite unlike the ordinary Cavendish varieties.
keyIngredients: The chuối ngự trắng, chuối ngự trâu or chuối ngự mít varieties
Alluvial soil along the Châu Giang river
prepOutline: Grow the bananas on the alluvial flats along the river, tending them by inherited family method
Choose a mature bunch and cut it down as the fruit starts to plump up
Let the bananas ripen naturally over a few days until the skin colours evenly yellow
Keep them somewhere cool and airy to hold the fragrance until they are eaten
chuoi-ngu-dai-hoang.howToEat: Chuối ngự is eaten as it is once just ripe, and is often set on the five-fruit tray and given as a fine gift at Tết for its clean sweetness and distinctive fragrance.

banh-cuon-phu-ly.description: Bánh cuốn Phủ Lý is the well-known breakfast dish of Phủ Lý city in Hà Nam, set apart by sheets spread in two passes from tám xoan rice flour — wafer-thin yet chewy. It is usually eaten with chả (pork patties) grilled over than hoa (charcoal) and with chả quế (cinnamon-scented pork sausage), which gives it a richer flavour of its own compared with bánh cuốn Thanh Trì or the egg-filled bánh cuốn of Hà Nội.
keyIngredients: Tám xoan rice flour (a fragrant northern rice variety)
Grilled chả (pork patties) or chả quế (cinnamon-scented pork sausage)
Sweet-sour mixed nước mắm (Vietnamese fish sauce)
prepOutline: Soak the tám xoan rice and grind it to a smooth batter
Spread the sheet in two thin layers over the steamer so it comes out translucent and chewy
Roll the sheets around a filling of wood ear mushroom and fragrant fried shallot
Arrange them with the grilled chả (pork patties) and pour over the sweet-sour nước mắm (Vietnamese fish sauce)
banh-cuon-phu-ly.howToEat: The bánh cuốn is eaten hot straight off the steamer, dipped in the sweet-sour nước mắm (Vietnamese fish sauce) with grilled chả (pork patties) alongside — the everyday breakfast of Phủ Lý locals.
